chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Hakam ibn Ayman, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever performs Tawaf of the House (Kaaba) for seven circuits, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will write for him six thousand good deeds, erase from him six thousand sins, and elevate him by six thousand degrees.'
He said: And Is'hak ibn 'Ammar added to it: 'And He will fulfill for him six thousand needs.'
He said: Then he said: 'And fulfilling the need of a believer is superior to performing Tawaf and Tawaf,' until he counted ten.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards of performing seven circuits of Tawaf and fulfilling a believer's need?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to illustrate the hierarchy of worship, contrasting the ritualistic merit of Tawaf with the social virtue of serving the community. The addition by Isma'il ibn Hammad regarding the cancellation of debts and fulfillment of needs underscores the Shia emphasis on 'qada' al-hajat' (meeting the needs of others) as a superior act of devotion that bridges the gap between individual piety and communal solidarity.
